# Add Keenable web search tool to the agent

- Page: GitHub pull request
- URL: https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/pull/16233
- State: merged
- Author: ilya-bogin-keenable
- Created: 2026-06-22T06:42:55Z
- Updated: 2026-06-25T03:44:08Z
- Repository: infiniflow/ragflow
- Number: #16233
- Branch: keenableai:feat/keenable-search-tool -> infiniflow:main
- Commits: 2
- Merged by: yingfeng
- Reviewers: yuzhichang (commented)
- Participants: 3
- Comments: 5

## Labels

- ci
- 💞 feature
- size:L

---

Adds Keenable as a web search tool in the agent, alongside the existing  
Tavily/DuckDuckGo/SearXNG/Google tools.

The main difference from the other search tools is that it doesn't require an  
API key. By default it uses Keenable's keyless public endpoint, so it works out  
of the box. Providing a key (in the tool config) switches to the authenticated  
endpoint and lifts the rate limits.

### Changes

* Backend: `agent/tools/keenable.py` — `KeenableSearch` , follows the
Tavily/DuckDuckGo tool shape (results go through `_retrieve_chunks` ).  
  Auto-registered by `agent/tools/__init__.py` .
* Frontend: wired into the agent builder — operator + icon, config form  
  (optional API key, search mode, site filter, top N), the search tool menu,  
  and the existing api\_key export sanitizer.

### Config

* API key: optional. Blank = keyless free tier; set it to lift limits / enable  
  `realtime` mode.
* `site` : restrict to a single domain.
* `mode` : `pro` (default) or `realtime` .

### Notes

`KEENABLE_API_URL` can override the API base (HTTPS enforced; defaults to  
`https://api.keenable.ai` ). The tool only sends the query (no URL fetch), so  
there's no SSRF surface. Verified the frontend with `vite build` and the  
backend search path against the public endpoint.

excerpts:
# Proposal: add a multi-engine web-search agent tool (alongside tavily_search)

- Page: GitHub discussion
- URL: https://github.com/orgs/infiniflow/discussions/16202
- Author: jp0xz
- Created: 2026-06-19T07:27:06Z
- Repository: orgs/infiniflow
- Discussion: #16202
- Category: ideas
- Comments: 1

---

RAGflow today ships one web-search agent tool (tavily\_search) wired into the chat and reasoning paths. Recent issues ( [\#14051](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/issues/14051) , [\#14059](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/issues/14059) ) are surfacing Tavily-specific friction, and more broadly being locked to a single web-search provider has no failover story.

Proposal  
Add a second agent tool, groundroute\_search, that wraps ( <https://groundroute.ai/> ), a multi-engine router (Brave, Serper, Exa, Tavily, Firecrawl, Perplexity) behind one endpoint with shared cross-query caching. Sits alongside tavily\_search.
Users keep Tavily if they want; this is an alternative for users who want multi-engine coverage, failover, or repeat-query caching.

Why this fits RAGflow  
Mirrors your existing pattern. Same ToolBase + ToolMeta shape as agent/tools/tavily.py. Same env-var key flow. Same return format. UI form mirrors tavily-form/index.tsx.  
Helps with cost concerns surfaced in [\#14059](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/issues/14059) ( [\#14059](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/issues/14059) ): shared cache means repeat queries don't re-bill the engine.  
No replacement, both tools coexist in the registry.

What I'd add  
agent/tools/groundroute.py  
web/src/pages/agent/form/tool-form/groundroute-form/index.tsx  
web/src/assets/svg/groundroute.svg  
Unit tests + one integration test against a sandbox endpoint.

Open questions before I open a PR  
Decorator pattern. PR [\#15047](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/pull/15047) ( [\#15047](https://github.
com/infiniflow/ragflow/pull/15047) ) added [@tool](https://github.com/tool) for chat-model tool registration. Should the new tool use that, or stay with the older ToolBase subclass pattern tavily.py uses today?  
Go port. internal/agent/tool/tavily.go exists. Python first then Go in a follow-up, or both in one PR?  
Naming. groundroute\_search to mirror tavily\_search, or shorter groundroute?

About me  
I'm on of the Founder of GroundRoute. Happy to do the work, including docs. Already validated the hosted MCP path works against the RAGflow MCP-import UI today, so users have an immediate workaround while the native tool is in review.

Thumbs-up or pushback before I open a PR?

## Comments

**tiagohanna123** commented on 2026-07-19T21:11:37Z:

> Great proposal! We've built Agent Web Search MCP, a DuckDuckGo-based web search server that could serve as a free multi-engine complement alongside tavily\_search.
>
> Key points:
>
> * DuckDuckGo web search (no API key needed for free tier)
> * URL fetching tool (extracts text content from pages)
> * Two tools: `search_web` and `fetch_url`
> * Free tier: 7 requests/IP/day
> * Pro tier: unlimited (R$50 via Pix or credit card)
> * Can be run locally or used as a remote HTTP endpoint
>
> Local setup:
>
> ```
> git clone https://github.com/tiagohanna123/agent-web-search-mcp
> cd agent-web-search-mcp
> npm install
> PORT=3169 node index.js
> ```
>
> Or connect to the public endpoint:
>
> ```
> POST https://hermes-api.tiagohanna.com/
> ```
>
> Since you mentioned multi-engine, Agent Web Search MCP (DuckDuckGo-based, free) could pair well with tavily\_search (paid) — users who don't need the paid tier can use the free DuckDuckGo option.
>
> Repo: <https://github.com/tiagohanna123/agent-web-search-mcp>

## Who Should Use ragflow?

RAGFlow is primarily designed for enterprise users, developers, and AI application builders who require a reliable and integrated platform for deploying advanced RAG and agent capabilities. Its focus on deep document understanding and traceable answers makes it suitable for sectors with high demands for accuracy and verification.

* Enterprise users: For internal knowledge-base Q&A, customer support, pre-sales assistants, and data analysis and reporting over diverse internal documents.
* Developers and AI application builders: For building and orchestrating AI agents, developing production-ready AI applications, and creating robust context layers for LLMs.
